statement_record.book: If D is small-complete, has small hom-sets, has a small cogenerating set Q, and every set of subobjects of each object of D has an intersection, then D has an initial object — namely the intersection r of all subobjects of the product q0 = ∏_{q∈Q} q. (Uniqueness of r → d from a proper-equalizer-subobject argument; existence by pulling the monic j : d → ∏_H q back along k : q0 → ∏_H q.)
statement_record.intree: Lemma cogenerator_canonical_monic ... : Monic (cogen_canonical comp G c).  — and, separately and with different hypotheses — Theorem initial_from_weakly_initial `(W : WeaklyInitialFamily C) (P : Limit ...) (Pe : Limit ...) (E : HasEqualizers C) : @Initial C.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: no in-tree statement concludes an initial object from small-completeness + a cogenerating set + intersections. What is present is (a) the hypothesis vocabulary [Cogenerator] / [SubobjectIndex], and (b) exactly one step of Mac Lane's proof — 'since Q cogenerates, the canonical map into the power of the family is monic' — proved in full as [cogenerator_canonical_monic] and genuinely consuming [cog_separates]. The only initial-object production theorem in the tree, [initial_from_weakly_initial], has the *V.6* (GAFT) hypothesis of a weakly initial family plus two Type-indexed products and equalizers; that hypothesis is neither implied by nor implies Theorem 1's, and its construction (joint equalizer of all endomorphisms of the product) is a different construction from Theorem 1's (intersection of all subobjects of the cogenerator product).

gap: The theorem itself is unstated. Three specific pieces are missing: (1) the intersection of a *family* of subobjects — the library has no wide pullback / no intersection operation at all; [Structure/Pullback.v:94] only remarks in prose that a binary pullback of two monos is an intersection of subobjects, and nothing constructs a limit of an arbitrary family of monos into a fixed object; (2) the uniqueness half of Theorem 1 (two distinct r → d would have an equalizer that is a strictly smaller subobject of q0 than the intersection) — no such argument exists in-tree; (3) the conclusion, an `Initial D` derived from `Complete D` + `Cogenerator D` + intersections. In-tree SAFT (Adjunction/SAFT.v:274) deliberately bypasses Theorem 1 entirely, routing instead through GAFT's solution-set / weakly-initial construction with the image-factorization step supplied as the caller-provided datum [SubobjectCover].

statement_record.book: Let A be small-complete with small hom-sets and a small cogenerating set Q, and suppose every set of subobjects of an object of A has a pullback (hence an intersection); let X have small hom-sets. Then G : A → X has a left adjoint IF AND ONLY IF G preserves all small limits and all pullbacks of families of monics. (Sufficiency by constructing an initial object in each comma (x ↓ G) via Theorem 1; necessity because right adjoints preserve limits.)

statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker on three axes and intree-stronger on one. STRONGER on the preservation axis: [cont] asks U to preserve ALL limits cone-level (PreservesImageLimit), not merely small limits and pullbacks of families of monics.

statement_record.book: A is well-powered when for each object a the subobjects of a can be indexed by a small set: there is a small set J_a and a BIJECTION from J_a onto the set of all subobjects of a. Dually co-well-powered (quotient objects of each object form a small set). Consequence recorded: A well-powered and small-complete ⇒ every set of subobjects of an object has an intersection, formed by pullback, so the extra hypothesis of Theorems 1 and 2 is automatic.
statement_record.intree: Record SubobjectIndex {C : Category} (x : C) := { sub_index : Type; sub_dom : sub_index -> C; sub_mono : forall i, sub_dom i ~> x; sub_monic : forall i, Monic (sub_mono i) }.  Well-poweredness of C is (informally, in the header only) [forall x, SubobjectIndex x].
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker in a way that matters. (1) SubobjectIndex demands only a Type-indexed FAMILY of monos into x; it never requires the indexing to be surjective onto (let alone bijective with) the subobjects of x, so the empty family trivially inhabits it. Mac Lane's definition is a bijection onto ALL subobjects of a. (2) It is not a named class: 'well-powered' exists only as header prose, never as a definition [WellPowered C]. (3) The library's own header admits the field is inert: 'The existence proof does not consume [sub_monic] — smallness is supplied here as data, not derived'. (4) Theory/Subobject.v's SubObj x carries the genuine subobject setoid (monos modulo domain isomorphism over x) — the right object to ask smallness of — but nothing anywhere relates SubObj x to SubobjectIndex x or asserts any smallness of it.

gap: Three missing pieces: (a) the exhaustiveness/bijectivity clause — no in-tree statement says that the chosen index enumerates ALL subobjects of x, so `SubobjectIndex` is a strictly weaker predicate than well-poweredness (it is trivially satisfiable); (b) the dual notion co-well-powered (quotient objects) does not exist anywhere in the tree; (c) the recorded consequence 'well-powered + small-complete ⇒ every set of subobjects has an intersection' is absent, since no intersection/wide-pullback construction exists at all.

Definition PreservesImageLimit : Type := ∀ (J : Category) (G : J ⟶ C) (L : Limit G) (N : Cone (U ◯ G)), ∃! φ : vertex_obj[N] ~{D}~> U L, ∀ x : J, image_leg L x ∘ φ ≈ cone_leg N x.

statement_record.book: Corollary (classical SAFT). If A is small-complete, well-powered, with small hom-sets and a small cogenerating set, and X has small hom-sets, then G : A → X has a left adjoint if and only if G is continuous (preserves all small limits). In particular every continuous functor K : A → Set is representable.
statement_record.intree: Definition SAFT ... (comp : @Complete C) (cont : @PreservesImageLimit C D U) (G : Cogenerator C) (WP : forall x : C, SubobjectIndex x) (cover : SubobjectCover U comp G WP) : { F : D ⟶ C & F ⊣ U }.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the corollary's whole point is that well-poweredness alone suffices — the intersections hypothesis of Theorem 2 is discharged from well-poweredness + completeness, and 'preserves pullbacks of families of monics' collapses into plain continuity. Neither discharge happens in-tree: [SAFT] still carries an extra hypothesis [cover] that the book DERIVES, so the corollary's exact hypothesis set never yields the conclusion. Additionally only the (⇐) direction exists (no iff), and the second sentence — every continuous K : A ⟶ Sets is representable — has no in-tree counterpart at all: [Representable] is defined but no theorem ever produces an instance from limit preservation.

gap: Two distinct pieces missing. (1) The reduction 'well-powered + small-complete ⇒ every family of subobjects has an intersection', which is what turns Theorem 2 into this corollary — the library has no intersection/wide-pullback construction, and its `SubobjectIndex` carries no exhaustiveness clause, so the reduction is not even statable as-is. (2) The representability half: no theorem 'K : A ⟶ Sets continuous (on a complete well-powered A with a cogenerating set) ⇒ Representable K'. Also, as with V.8:thm2, no iff is assembled from the separately-proved necessity ([right_adjoint_PreservesImageLimit]).
